title: Stability SLO Gating Playbook & Staggered Rollout
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic cross-functional playbook for introducing gated SLO-driven rollouts across model serving and API routes. It defines the gating criteria, phased rollout plan, stakeholders, metrics to monitor, and the decision cadence for moving services from pilot -> staggered -> wide rollout.

Audience:
SREs, Platform Eng, Serving Runtime, Product (Hosted API + Dedicated), Observability, Solutions Eng, Customer Success.

Summary / TL;DR:
- We will pilot enforceable SLO gates on 3 representative services (stateless text-gen, chat session proxy, embeddings ingestion) for 10 weeks.
- Gate checks run daily; move to next phase only if SLO pass + error-budget burn <= threshold + observability coverage >= 80%.
- Staggered rollout uses 4 waves by traffic segment (internal-only -> low-traffic external -> medium -> high & canary).
- Primary success metric: sustained SLO attainment for 30 days post-rollout with error budget consumption < 30% per 30 day window.

Scope & Boundaries:
In scope: API surface (generation/chat/embeddings) served by hosted and dedicated, runtime kernel selection paths, autoscaling triggers that affect latency, and observability instrumentation (traces/metrics/logs).
Out of scope: billing/quotas product changes, major model architecture changes (those get separate gating).

Why this approach?
- We have inconsistent SLO adoption across teams; past rollouts failed because we bumped traffic without clear rollback triggers.
- Using a repeatable gating mechanism reduces blast radius and gives product teams confidence.

Primary Objectives (measurable):
- 95th-pct latency SLO defined and adopted for three pilot services within 2 weeks.
- Observability (tracing + latency histograms + error rates) coverage >=80% for endpoints in pilot.
- Zero customer-facing incidents caused by rollout during pilot period.
- Documented rollback and canary procedures in the repo.

SLO definitions (example):
- Generation API: P95 latency <= 300ms for downstream route (small context). Error rate (5xx) < 0.5% per 24h.
- Chat proxy: P99 latency <= 700ms (includes KV ops). Error rate < 1% per 24h.
- Embeddings ingestion: Throughput SLO: 1,200 reqs/min sustained for burst windows; latency P95 <= 2000ms; error rate < 0.2%.

Error budget policy (gating):
- Gate pass if the 30-day error-budget burn rate < 30%.
- For daily checkpoints during rollout, rolling 7d burn < 50% to proceed to next wave.
- If burn > 75% in any 24h window, immediate rollback to previous stable config and SRE war-room.

Observability Gate:
- Metrics: latency histograms, per-route QPS, 5xx/4xx counts, tail-quantiles, cache hit rates, batch sizes.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces for >=80% of requests (sampling + service-span propagation confirmed).
- Alerts: alerts fire and page on pre-defined thresholds (see linked alerts in JIRA SRE-402).

Phased Rollout Plan (high level):
Phase 0 — Discovery (Week 0–2):
- Inventory routes, map owners, collect current SLOs; instrumentation gap analysis.
- Deliverable: SLO draft doc per service, instrumentation checklist.
Owners: Aisha (SRE lead), Emily (observability).

Phase 1 — Pilot (Week 3–6):
- Choose 3 pilot services (see summary). Create canary configs and test harnesses.
- Run synthetic load + 10% traffic mirror for 7 days. Gate opens daily at 10:00 UTC.
- Runbook: documented in repo /playbooks/stability-pilot.md.
Owners: Service owners + SRE oncall.

Phase 2 — Staggered rollout (Week 7–12):
- Wave A (internal + staging): 48h observation window, gate check at 24h/48h.
- Wave B (low-traffic customers): 7d observation, check gates, if pass -> next.
- Wave C (medium traffic): 14d observation.
- Wave D (high traffic + global region): full verification and SLO burn review.
Owners: Platform Eng (autoscale), Product (routing policy), SRE (gate decisions).

Phase 3 — Wide rollout & operationalize (Week 13+):
- Bake the gating logic into deployment pipelines (CI job that queries metrics + approves).
- Train oncall + runbooks; add dashboards to Redwood Console public internal folder.

Daily/Weekly Cadence and Decision Flow:
- Daily: automated gate check report posted to #sre-stability-thread at 09:00 UTC. If any threshold violated, SRE lead pings service owner and incident war-room may be opened.
- Weekly: cross-functional sync (30–45m) to review pilot metrics, actionable items, and backlog. Attendees: SRE lead, Service owners, Observability, Platform Eng, Product PM.
- Go/No-Go: For each wave, decision is explicit in meeting notes and recorded as JIRA workflow transition (RDINF-1289 -> status: gate-passed).

Gating Criteria (detailed):
- Instrumentation: metrics + traces coverage >=80% AND synthetic tests green for 48h.
- SLOs: 30d rolling attainment above target; 7d burn <50%.
- Safety: fallback route & autoscale tested; rollback runbook validated (time to revert <10m for config toggles).
- Customer Impact: no degradation on top-5 revenue customers during the window.

Rollback Triggers & Playbook (short):
- Immediate rollback if 24h error budget burn >75% OR customer P0 reported latency/availability regression.
- Revert traffic routing to previous variant; disable new kernel/quantization path; restore model pin if changed.
- War-room lead: SRE oncall; Communication owner: Product PM (template in Confluence).

Risks and Mitigations:
- Risk: Observability blindspots (false positives/negatives). Mitigation: run synthetic + real traffic mirrors, add temporary increased sampling.
- Risk: Autoscale policy interacts with latency SLOs unpredictably. Mitigation: test in staging with workload replay, tune scale cooldowns.
- Risk: Upstream dependencies (DB, KV) cause tail latencies. Mitigation: SLOs include dependency impact tags; contract owners to monitor.

Runbook snippets / checklist (copy into runbook):
- Pre-wave checklist: instrumentation verified, rollback toggles present, traffic split config ready, alerting active, runbook assigned.
- During-wave checklist: monitor SLO dashboards, track error-budget consumption hourly for first 24h, test rollback path.
- Post-wave checklist: retro note, update SLO thresholds if necessary, record learnings.

Measurement plan & dashboards:
- Dashboards: per-route SLO view (P50/P95/P99), burn rate chart, top contributing error classes, request sample traces.
- Export: daily gate-check CSV for audit. Store in /observability/reports/stability-YYYYMMDD.csv.
- Postmortems: attach to the JIRA ticket for the rollout wave.

Open action items (owner / estimate):
- Implement gate-check CI job (Rajiv / 2w).
- Add route-level P99 histograms to metrics export (Emily / 1w).
- Create synthetic traffic harness for embeddings (Tomás / 2w).
- Customer comms template for rollout (Laura / 3d).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider building an automated “slo-gate” GitHub action that reads metrics and posts approval -> reduces meeting overhead.
- Could test a ‘graceful degradation’ policy where heavy requests get queued but cheaper fallback model served. Needs product buy-in.
- Keep waves short early to learn quickly.

Communication Plan:
- Internal: gate-check posts to #sre-stability-thread; weekly report to eng leadership; postmortem and lessons in Confluence.
- Customer: for waves that touch customers, send a short note via CSM with opt-out instructions for first 48h.

Appendix: Useful links and templates
- SLO template (paste into Confluence): service, route, SLO name, target, measurement window, owner, alert threshold, rollback threshold.
- Example alerting rules: high-tail-latency (P99 > threshold x 3), error-rate-surge (> baseline*5).
- Template JIRA sub-tasks for rollout steps (RDINF-1289 linked).

Final checklist before publishing this playbook (TODO):
- [ ] Align with Product legal for customer comms wording.
- [ ] Dry-run of rollback on staging with live load.
- [ ] Confirm telemetry retention for 30d for all pilot routes.

If you're reading this and want to change any metric or gate — call it out in the weekly sync. This should be a lightweight, living playbook, not a heavyweight gate that blocks necessary experiments.

-- Aisha (drafted 2026-11-15, updated 2026-12-02)
